full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that, respondent No.1 herein as petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No.13 of 1997 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Burichang Comilla under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption against the opposite parties stating that, the case land appertaining to CS Khatian No.129 originally belonged to Baksa Ali and Bangu Gazi in equal shares, and, that Baksa Ali died before CS operation leaving behind widow, Diljan Bibi, 3 sons namely, Minnat Ali, Zinnat Ali, and, Aham Ali and one daughter, Maleka Bibi. The name of Maleka Bibi was wrongly omitted in the CS khatian, and, that Diljan Bibi died leaving behind the aforesaid sans and daughter as her heirs. Aham Ali died leaving behind Mohar Ali, who, sold his share to Sayed Ali, Keramat Ali and Suzat Ali. Minnat Ali died leaving behind Zunab Ali, Syed Ali, and, pre-emptee No.3 as three sons, and, pre-emptee No.4 as daughter, and, during RS Operation, the land of CS Khatian No.129 was recorded in three separate Khatians, one Khatian in the name of the heirs of Bengu Gazi, another in the name of purchasers from the heirs of Baksa Ali Khatian No.128 was prepared in the name of Minnat Ali, Zinnat Ali and Maleka Bibi, Zinnat Ali gifted his share to his wife Kamalijan, who, subsequently gifted the same to her daughter, the pre-emptee No.2. Zunab Ali and Shaun Ali, sons of Minnat Ali, sold their shares to the pre-emptee No.5. Maleka Bibi died leaving behind Syed Ali, Shiraj Ali, Roshan Ali and one daughter, the pre-emptee No.13. Syed Ali died leaving behind two sons, the pre-emptee Nos.6 and 7. Roshan Ali died leaving behind the pre-emptor and pre-emptee Nos.9 and 10 as three sons, pre-emptee No.8 as widow and pre-emptee Nos.11 and 12 as two daughter. Shiraj Meah died leaving behind the pre-emptee Nos.14 and 15. The pre-emptor is the co-sharer in the case jute, and, the pre-emptee No.1 is a stranger purchaser from pre-emptee No.2 vide registered deed dated 8-3-1993. The disputed sale, and, receipt of a certified copy of 26-4- 1997, he came to know that, the pre-emptee Nos.2 got 9 decimals of land from the pre-emptee No.1 in exchange of his 35 decimals of land, and, the pre-emptee No.2 transferred the said 9 decimals of land to the son of pre-emptee No.1 vide registered deed dated 24-3-1994, and, the disputed deed in fact is a sale deed, and, not an exchange deed created from the purpose of avoiding pre-emption, and, the pre-emptee No.2 has no possession in the alleged exchanged land, and, the pre-emptor being cultivator is entitled to get the case land by way of pre-emption. Hence the case. 

 3. The pre-emptee No.1 contested the said case by filing a written objection denying the material allegations made in the pre-emption petition contending, inter-alia, that, Baksa Ali was owner of the case land in Khatian No.129. Simlarly Baksa. Ali died leaving behind Diljan Bibi as widow, Zinnat Ali, Minnat Ali, Aham Ali as three sons, and, Maleka Bibi as daughter. Dilijan Bibi died leaving behind the aforesaid sons, and daughter. Maleka Bibi in the aforesaid two khatians inherited 56% decimals land by amicable partition, and, she gifted the same to her nephews, Zunab Ali, Shazan Ali, Keramat Ali, and thus, Maleka Bibi having transferred more than her shares her heirs did not inherit anything in the case khatian, and, the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the case Khatian. The further case of the pre-emptee is that, the pre-emptee No.2 in exchange of his 35 decimals of land got 9 decimals from the pre-emptee No.1, and, sold the case land to the pre-emptee No.16 vide registered deed for a consideration of Taka 25,000, and, the pre-emptee No.2 also sold 9 decimals to the sons of pre-emptee No.1 vide registered deed dated 24-3-1994, and, as such, for that reasons, the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed with Costs. 

 17. I t is evident from the certified copies of the CS and SA Khatian of the case land produced by the contesting pre-emptee that the pre-emptor filed the case as a co-sharer by inheritance in the case Khatians and it appears from those Khatians that all the admitted co-sharers are not made party in the case although the PW 1 mentioned their names in his examination in chief, lf so, although no objection was raised to this effect but as per evidence adduced by the parties it is clear that the suit is bad for defect of parties but the High Court Division non-considering the same reversed the findings of the last court of fact.
